memory_candidates.content: When an agent's own report/summary skeleton is being audited for validate-artifact.sh conformance, check the skeleton in isolation (the fenced block only), not the whole file: the validator's metadata check is `grep -qF "**Field**:"` (whole-document, literal substring) and the section check is `grep -qE "^##+ Section"` (whole-document, prefix-match at any heading depth) -- both can produce false positives from an agent-authoring-prose hit (e.g. a Context References bullet mentioning '**Standards**:') that never reaches the produced artifact. Scope every verification grep to the fenced ```markdown ... ``` skeleton block itself, e.g. `awk '/^## Stage N: .../{f=1} f && /^```markdown$/{c=1;next} f && c && /^```$/{exit} f && c' file.md`.

Before running a same-repo 'redeploy and diff source vs. .claude/' verification step for an extension-specific agent file, confirm the extension is actually installed/active in that repo's .claude-extensions.json. deploy-headless.sh only resyncs extensions the state file already marks active -- it will not deploy a source-store agent file for an extension the current repo never installed, so `.claude/agents/<file>.md` will simply be absent and a diff step will silently have nothing to compare against. When this happens, close the phase with a `#### Reasoned Exclusions` record (evidence: the .claude-extensions.json extensions list, plus `ls .claude/agents/`) and defer the deployed-copy verification to whichever phase/repo actually has the extension installed, rather than forcing the check or leaving the phase open indefinitely.
